# werkbord

> werkbord is a local-first team workspace for AI agents. Plan and approve the work on one board. Claude Code and Codex do the work in their own Git worktrees, and nothing merges without a person.

## Page

- [werkbord](https://micho8cho93.github.io/werkbord-site/): the headline, a beta waitlist with a live count of the first 50 places, and a guided demo of the app at desktop and phone width: your work across workspaces in Universal, Salie (with next-step suggestions that cite what it remembers, and personal workspaces it generates and saves on your computer), agents running in parallel, review and merge, and a Team (claims, comments and @mentions), with projects, analytics, settings and help to open; the phone demo follows the app's Control Deck layout.

## Facts on the page

- werkbord is a local-first team workspace for AI agents. People plan and approve the work on one board. Agents do the work in their own Git worktrees, one per task.
- werkbord is a meta-harness: a layer between the person and all of their agents. Each agent is a harness around a model; werkbord coordinates them in one workspace, with tasks, Git branches and memory together.
- Claude Code and Codex work with werkbord today, through their own command-line tools and the user's own accounts.
- Nothing merges without a person. Agents do not merge their own work.
- Beta: the first 50 people to sign up get beta access. It covers individual and team apps.
- The waitlist asks for an email address and, optionally, the team size: 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6 or more.
- The demo runs in the page on a made-up repository and a made-up team. It needs no install. The Team part is early access.

## Planned, not available today

- Support for AI models other than Claude Code and Codex.
